title: A flat finite type cover has local sections after a finite normalization of a semi-trait
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one with finitely many maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], put $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $f:T\to S$ be a flat surjective morphism of finite presentation between affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. There exists a finite field extension $L/K$ [def-pc-field-extension] such that, writing $R_L$ for the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] and $S_L=\operatorname{Spec}R_L$, there is a finite Zariski open covering $S_L=\bigcup_{j=1}^n U_j$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and an $S$-morphism $u_j:U_j\to T$ for each $j$. Equivalently, the base change $T\times_SS_L\to S_L$ has a section over each $U_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. No separability of $L/K$ or module-finiteness of $R_L/R$ is required.

source.place: Tag 05GU, lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X, the integral quasi-section input; fields.tex Tag 09DT, lemma-normal-closure; integral-closure prime conjugacy as in more-algebra.tex Tag 0BRI, lemma-one-orbit (with the purely inseparable part retained). These give the geometric construction in Anantharaman Lemma 4.2.1, second paragraph, printed p.56; local Anantharaman archive WANTED.

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$. By definition a morphism of finite presentation is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], so by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] the ring map $\mathcal O_S(V)\to\mathcal O_T(U)$ is of finite presentation, in particular of finite type, for every pair of affine opens $U\subseteq T$, $V\subseteq S$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$. Hence $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], and ($U=T$, $V=S$) $B$ is finitely generated over $R$. The affine flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] makes $B$ flat over $R$. For each maximal ideal $m$ of $R$, surjectivity makes $T_m$ nonempty. Its affine coordinate ring is $B\otimes_R R/m=B/mB$ [lem-sbc-affine-fibre-sections-tensor]. This ring is nonzero, since the nonempty scheme $T_m$ has nonzero global sections. Choose a maximal ideal $\bar n$ of $B/mB$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]; its preimage $n\subset B$ is a maximal ideal of $B$ containing $mB$ (as $B/n\cong(B/mB)/\bar n$ is a field), so $n\cap R=m$. Its point $x_m\in T$ lies over $m$ and is closed in $T$, hence closed in the fibre $T_m$. Finally $\{\eta\}$ is open in $S$: choose $0\ne r_m\in m$ for each of the finitely many maximal ideals and set $r=\prod_mr_m\ne0$. Since $R$ is a one-dimensional domain, every nonzero prime is maximal, and $D(r)=\{\eta\}$. Thus $T_\eta$ is an open subscheme of $T$.

source.place: Tag 05GU: preparation for the nearby-open quasi-section; affine fibre and prime-ideal argument written out.

proof.text: Fix $m$. By [lem-sc-flat-going-down], the prime of $x_m$ in $B$ contains a prime contracting to $(0)\subset R$. Its point $x'_m$ lies in $T_\eta$ and specializes to $x_m$. The scheme $S$ is locally Noetherian by its single affine chart [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-sfb-quasi-section-nearby-open] to $T\to S$, $x_m$ and the open $T_\eta$: the finite-type hypothesis, the closed-fibre-point hypothesis and the distinct-image nearby point have all been supplied. It gives an integral closed subscheme $Z_m\subseteq T$ through $x_m$, whose generic point maps to $\eta$, with $Z_m\to S$ quasi-finite at $x_m$.

source.place: Tag 05GU, lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X; flat going down is algebra.tex Tag 00HS.

proof.text: The quasi-finite locus in $Z_m$ is open [lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open]. Since $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, the closed immersion $Z_m\subset T$ gives $Z_m=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I_m)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Choose a principal affine neighbourhood $W_m=D(h_m)=\operatorname{Spec}D_m$ of $x_m$ inside the quasi-finite locus [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open, lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], and restrict the locally quasi-finite map to it [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens]. Explicitly $D_m=(B/I_m)[1/h_m]$ is generated over $R$ by the images of generators of $B$ and by $1/h_m$, so is finite type. Because $Z_m$ is integral and dominates $S$, [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] makes $D_m$ a domain, and $R\to D_m$ is injective: a nonzero kernel would force the whole image into a proper $V(a)\subset S$. Its generic fibre algebra $D_m\otimes_RK=(R\setminus0)^{-1}D_m$ [lem-sbc-affine-fibre-sections-tensor] is a nonzero domain, finite-dimensional over $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-qc-source-bounded-fibres], since $W_m$ is affine and quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. It is therefore a field $E_m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], and is the fraction field of $D_m$. Thus $E_m/K$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 01TI, lemma-quasi-finite-points-open; Tag 03JA, lemma-locally-quasi-finite-qc-source; affine fibre localization and finite-domain field argument.

proof.text: Let $C_m$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $D_m$, and $A_m$ its integral closure in $E_m$. Since $W_m$ is affine, the map $W_m\to S$ is separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]; it is of finite type, and everywhere quasi-finite; $S$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [pqf-lem-normalization-open] and the affine description [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]: the factorization $W_m\to\operatorname{Spec}C_m\to S$ identifies $W_m$ with an open subscheme, and its ring map is the inclusion $C_m\subseteq D_m$. We have $C_m\subseteq A_m\subseteq E_m$. Every element of $A_m$ satisfies a monic equation over $R\subset C_m$, so $C_m\hookrightarrow A_m$ is integral. Let $c_m$ be the prime in $C_m$ corresponding to $x_m$ in that open chart. Lying over [pqf-lem-lying-over] gives a prime $a_m$ of $A_m$ above $c_m$, hence above $m$. The inverse image $V_m\subset\operatorname{Spec}A_m$ of the open $W_m\subset\operatorname{Spec}C_m$ contains $a_m$ and has an $S$-map $v_m:V_m\to W_m\to T$. Here $A_m$ is a domain integral over $R$ with fraction field $E_m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal]; module-finiteness is never used.

source.place: Tag 02LR, lemma-quasi-finite-separated-quasi-affine; morphisms.tex Tags 035F, 035H, 035I give the affine integral-closure description; algebra.tex Tag 00GU gives lying over.

proof.text: The nonzero one-dimensional ring $R$ has a nonempty finite set of maximal ideals. Apply [lem-sfb-common-normal-compatible-groups] with base field $K$, fields $E_m$, and trivial groups $J_m$. Retain its finite normal extension $L/K$, embeddings $E_m\hookrightarrow L$ and finiteness of $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(L)$. Identify each $E_m$ with its image. Put $A=R_L\subset L$. The integral-closure theorem [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal] says that $A$ is a domain integral over $R$ with fraction field $L$. There are compatible inclusions $C_m\subset A_m\subset A$; again $A_m\to A$ is integral since each element of $A$ is integral already over $R$. By [pqf-lem-lying-over], $a_m$ lifts to a prime $b_m\subset A$. The inverse image $O_m$ of $V_m$ under $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A_m$ contains $b_m$, lies over $m$ there, and carries the composite $S$-map $w_m:O_m\to V_m\to T$.

source.place: Tag 09DT, lemma-normal-closure, finite normal common envelope as supplied by the existing simultaneous-envelope node; algebra.tex Tag 00GU for lifting the chart point.

proof.text: For each $m$, $R_m$ is a DVR by [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr]. Its integral closure in $L$ is $A^{(m)}=(R\setminus m)^{-1}A$. Here is the localization calculation: every $a/s$ with $a\in A$, $s\notin m$, is integral over $R_m$ by dividing a monic equation for $a$ by the corresponding powers of $s$. Conversely, if $z\in L$ satisfies $z^d+c_1z^{d-1}+\cdots+c_d=0$ over $R_m$, choose $s\in R\setminus m$ clearing the finitely many coefficient denominators. Then $sz$ satisfies the monic equation with coefficients $s^ic_i\in R$, so $sz\in A$ and $z\in A^{(m)}$. Primes of $A$ contracting to $m$ correspond exactly to maximal ideals of $A^{(m)}$: extend such a prime by fractions and contract back, which are inverse because its denominators avoid the prime. The extension is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal]; conversely a maximal ideal contracts to the maximal ideal of $R_m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal], and thence to $m$.

source.place: Tag 034X, lemma-characterize-Dedekind; Tag 0307, lemma-integral-closure-localize, whose denominator argument is written out here; integral prime/maximal correspondence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-coefficient-branch-conjugacy] with the identity local map of DVRs $R_m\to R_m$, both fraction fields $K$, and normal extension $N=L$. The reduced tensor algebra $(K\otimes_KL)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is $L$, and both integral closures in that statement are $A^{(m)}$ by step 6. Its conclusion therefore makes $G$ transitive on the maximal ideals of $A^{(m)}$, hence on the primes of $A$ above $m$. The action really is global on $A$: a $K$-automorphism carries any monic equation over $R$ to the same equation, so preserves $A$; on $A^{(m)}$ its action is the localization of this one, fixing the denominators in $R$. In particular, for every prime $b\subset A$ above $m$ there is a scheme automorphism $g$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ over $S$, induced by an element of $G$, with $g(b)=b_m$. Thus $b\in g^{-1}(O_m)$, and $w_m\circ g$ on this open is an $S$-morphism to $T$. No equality $L^G=K$ is asserted: the cited conjugacy result explicitly allows inseparable normal extensions.

source.place: Tag 09EU, lemma-galois-relative, specialized to the identity DVR extension; use the corrected possibly inseparable formulation of the cited node, rather than the erroneous fixed-field equality in the printed proof.

proof.text: There are only finitely many opens $g^{-1}(O_m)$, since the set of $m$ and the group $G$ are finite. They cover every maximal ideal $b$ of $A$: its contraction to $R$ is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal], and step 7 covers its fibre. Every prime $p$ of $A$ is contained in a maximal ideal $b$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]. The basic-open basis [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] shows that an open containing $b$ also contains $p$: a basic open $D(h)$ containing $b$ has $h\notin b$, hence $h\notin p$. Therefore the displayed finite family covers $S_L$. Enumerate it as $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ and take the maps $u_j$ constructed in step 7. By the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], pairing $u_j$ with $U_j\hookrightarrow S_L$ gives a section $U_j\to T\times_SS_L$ of its projection. Conversely composing a section with the projection to $T$ gives $u_j$. This proves both formulations with the original hypotheses.
